subtitle: 21 runs, 1.1M env steps each, size50m, one training seed per run. Every run scored on the same 30 fixed worlds (episode i built from seed i; one world hash across all runs) with tools/death_eval.py. Updated 2026-10-14.
summary:
Every number is the mean episode-final achievement count over 30 evaluation episodes, ± its standard error over those worlds; unlock rates are the share of episodes in which an achievement fired; return is the mean raw Craftax return as a % of the maximum (226). An outside audit (2026-10-11, docs/audit-2026-10-11.md) found that earlier evaluations only shared the first world: later worlds depended on how long earlier episodes ran. All checkpoints were re-scored on fixed worlds, so every comparison below is paired world by world. The error bars cover the worlds only, not training seeds -- every run is one seed.
The same audit found three RSSM-2 bugs (non-moves counted as a step down, a new episode inheriting the old one's state, and training seeing up to 7 future steps). Honest map, B2, v1.2 and v2 were retrained with every fix (bold rows). None improved: B2 8.27 vs 8.40, v2 7.17 vs 6.93, honest map 5.70 vs 6.17 -- all within noise -- and v1.2 fell from 9.97 to 8.77 (paired -1.20 ± 0.57), which one seed cannot tell apart from seed variation.
What holds up on the fixed code: masking impossible actions (B2 vs honest map +2.57 ± 0.48, t = 5.3); v2 over vanilla DreamerV3 (+2.53 ± 0.44, t = 5.8); the honest map over vanilla (+1.07 ± 0.24), though that run also has the potential shaping. What is not established: the manager over B2 (v1.2 fix vs B2 fix +0.50 ± 0.57), the order among v1.1/v1.2/v1.3, and curiosity (v2 vs v2-cur +0.40 ± 0.39). Two more training seeds of the fixed B2, v1.2 and v2 are running.
Normalized return, raw Craftax reward on the fixed worlds: best 4.04% (v1.2, old code), 3.48% for v1.2 fixed, 3.32% for B2, 2.77% for v2 fixed, 1.65% for vanilla DreamerV3, against 7.09% for ITC (transformer world model, pixels). The B2 and v1.x runs read the game's action rules and hand-written goals; v2 keeps only the action rules.
table_note: ach. ± SE = mean episode-final achievements ± standard error over the 30 worlds (one training seed, so seed variation is not included). w/o wake = the same minus WAKE_UP. life = mean lifespan in steps. return = raw Craftax return, % of 226. Rates are % of episodes. Bold rows were trained on the code with the RSSM-2 and shaping fixes of 2026-10-11; the others are the original checkpoints, re-scored. 'bug' = imag_shift True (fixed 2026-09-20). B1/B2: validity flags as an encoder input / impossible actions masked. mgr v1-v1.3: B2 plus the two-level agent (docs/design-manager.md). B3: the mask learned instead of read from the rules. v2: learned goals, curiosity, RSSM-2 as a memory, rule mask kept (docs/design-v2.md); v2-cur: v2 with curiosity actually scaled.

checkpoints.title: One run, four checkpoints: Map + potential (bug)
checkpoints.note: The same training run, scored at four points (25-30 episodes each), moves by 1.08 achievements. That is the scale of noise any comparison between single runs has to beat.

interpretation.heading: 0. Masking impossible actions is the one large, robust gain
interpretation.body: B2 beats the same model without the mask by +2.57 ± 0.48 achievements on the fixed code (+2.23 on the old), on the same 30 worlds. Buttons that were never pressed where they would work (the wood pickaxe, the furnace, placing stone) get pressed once a useless press can no longer teach the agent that the button is bad. The mask reads the game's rules, so it is a separate arm from the published, knowledge-free agents.

interpretation.heading: 1. The manager's lead is not established
interpretation.body: v1.2 scored 9.97 on the old code but 8.77 after the RSSM-2 fixes, and its lead over B2 on the fixed code is +0.50 ± 0.57. The old manager results were single seeds whose differences (v1.1 vs v1.2 vs v1.3) are all within noise on paired worlds. Two more seeds of B2, v1.2 and v2 will say whether the manager helps.

interpretation.heading: 2. v2 clearly beats vanilla DreamerV3 -- but not B2
interpretation.body: v2 drops the hand-written goals, the reward potentials and the map labels, and still beats vanilla by +2.53 ± 0.44 (fixed code). It stays at the wood tier: no stone tool in any episode. B2 leads it by +1.10 ± 0.59. Curiosity, once scaled (v2-cur), changed nothing measurable.

interpretation.heading: 3. The RSSM-2 fixes did not explain the results
interpretation.body: Training no longer sees future steps, episodes no longer leak, and non-moves no longer count as a step down. The fixed runs land within noise of the old ones (v1.2 aside). The map model's contribution was real but not driven by the leak.

interpretation.heading: 4. Survival is still unsolved
interpretation.body: Lifespans stay near the random band (255-320 steps); thirst, hunger and mobs still kill most episodes. The longest-living fixed run is v1.2 (319 steps), which crafts less than before.

interpretation.heading: 5. What would settle the rest
interpretation.body: Training seeds: three per arm for B2, v1.2 and v2 (two more each are queued), and ideally for vanilla. Then a knowledge-free comparison: v2 without the rule mask needs a mask that can tell "does nothing" from "not yet learned" (B3 and B3-fix could not).
